headline: High-risk pairwise conflicts are limited by B's no-network, no-IO profile; main residual issues are A's writable/tooling surface and compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can use MCP, stdin/stdout, shell, and subprocesses, so if B's content is manually copied into A or bridged through a shared channel, prompt injection is possible. B has no IO surfaces or network egress, so there is no documented automatic bridge from B to A; the pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies B-generated text into A's stdin/stdout or MCP inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, B content can reach A automatically.
mitigations: Keep B outputs out of A prompts unless manually reviewed.
Disable or restrict MCP routes that accept free-form text.
Use a one-way, human-reviewed handoff format.
Separate workspaces so B cannot write files A reads.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, while B touches no data classes and has no network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or upload path, so leakage from A to B is not a default pathway; the main risk is accidental manual transfer of sensitive A outputs into B workflows.
conditions: IF the operator pastes A outputs containing sensitive repository metadata into B-facing systems, leakage can occur.
IF a shared workspace is introduced and B begins reading files from it, A data may be exposed.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in A's prompts or outputs.
Keep B isolated from A's workspace and logs.
Review any copied artifacts before sharing them with B.
Turn off automatic transcript syncing between agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has shell, package install, git mutation, subprocess, and allowlisted network egress; B has no declared write or network capabilities. Direct write-write conflict is not shown, but A's mutable tooling can still collide with any external state B influences through orchestration, so uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF B is later given write access to the same repository or workspace, concurrent mutation conflicts become possible.
IF the orchestrator maps B recommendations into A's git or package actions, state collisions can occur.
mitigations: Serialize A's git and package operations.
Keep B read-only.
Use separate repositories or branches per agent.
Check for lockfiles before A mutates state.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate and modify artifacts via shell, git, and MCP, and B is a customer-support agent with no verification or action-taking controls shown. If B consumes A's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream responses or actions; the lack of documented verification makes medium appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced text or files without independent verification, cascading errors can propagate.
IF A's outputs are routed into customer-facing replies or tickets, incorrect facts can be amplified.
mitigations: Require B to cite source evidence before acting.
Add a human review step for A-generated claims.
Limit A outputs to structured data with validation rules.
Flag unsupported assertions in B before sending them onward.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles task prompts, repository metadata, and Ed25519 signatures, while B lists no data classes and no residency or retention controls. No explicit compliance mismatch is documented, so only a low-severity gap remains from unverified policies and the possibility that A's handled data could be routed into a less controlled B workflow.
conditions: IF A processes regulated data and B is used to store or relay it, policy mismatch risk increases.
IF B is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime different from A's, compliance gaps may emerge.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through B.
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents.
Review whether A's signatures or prompts are subject to policy controls.
Keep audit logs of inter-agent transfers.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies before deployment.
